name: grap
why: A tiny troff-era language for typesetting graphs, a forgotten Unix dialect that shows what plotting looked like before GUIs.

brief.what_it_is: Grap is a language for describing graphs so they can be typeset inside documents. It is a preprocessor: grap input is translated into Kernighan's pic language, and the pic output is then handled by whatever system runs pic. The page says TeX and groff can both use it. The page does not describe the exact input file format or the command-line usage.
brief.why_it_exists: Grap was specified and first implemented by Brian Kernighan and Jon Bentley at Bell Labs. Ted Faber says groff's James J. Clark did not implement grap when writing groff, and that he wrote it himself because he 'finally wanted to use it badly enough'.
brief.how_it_works: Grap is implemented as a preprocessor to pic, so any system that can use pic can use grap. The page does not describe the internal steps beyond this.
brief.install_notes: The page names no install steps beyond the source being available. Grap needs a pic-capable typesetting system to run, such as groff or TeX. The brew formula is named 'grap' and the executable is 'grap'. The brew caveats field is empty.
brief.standout: It is a small, old-school tool for typesetting graphs with troff and pic, not a GUI plotting package. Its own author calls it 'an expressive language for describing graphs'. It is still being updated, which is unusual for a tool from the Bell Labs troff era.
brief.status: Maintained, judging by the homepage. Version 1.49 was released 16 Apr 2025, and the author says it is 'probably worth upgrading to' because a bug in handling an undefined value was fixed. The scout note calls it 'forgotten', but the 2025 release suggests otherwise. The brief did not check the GitHub source or CHANGES file for later commits.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not mention supported platforms, the license, or the exact input syntax. Grap is not usable alone, since it depends on pic and a troff or TeX toolchain. The homepage was reachable, but the linked source and man pages were not fetched.

entry.title: grap
entry.tldr: A Bell Labs-era language for describing graphs as text and typesetting them inside troff or TeX documents, still being updated in 2025.
entry.deeper_look:
Grap is a small language for describing graphs so they can be dropped into typeset documents. It is a preprocessor: grap input is translated into pic, Kernighan's language for drawing diagrams, and whatever system runs pic takes it from there. The homepage says both groff and TeX can use it.

It was specified and first implemented by Brian Kernighan and Jon Bentley at Bell Labs. The free troff, groff, shipped without it. Ted Faber, who maintains this version, says of groff's author: "For some reason, when James J. Clark implemented groff, a free version of troff and associated tools, he didn't implement grap. I finally wanted to use it badly enough that I wrote it."

The idea underneath is the old Unix one: small languages that each do one job and feed the next. A graph is not a picture you draw with a mouse, it is a description that compiles to another description, which compiles to a page. Reading grap is a way into how troff-era documents were built, and why plotting once lived inside the typesetter.

The project is not frozen. Version 1.49 was released on 16 April 2025, with a fix for a mishandled undefined value. The author says it is "probably worth upgrading to".
entry.install:
brew install grap
# grap only emits pic code. To get a finished page you also need a pic-capable system such as groff or TeX.

entry.whats_unique: It is a graph language from the original Bell Labs troff toolchain, written as a text-to-text preprocessor for pic rather than as a plotting program with its own output. Its author still maintains it.
entry.caveats: It does nothing alone, since it needs pic and a troff or TeX toolchain, and the brief did not cover the input syntax, so expect to read the man pages.
